idiom_name: pthread_mutex + two pthread_cond_t conditions guarding a ring buffer
implementation_notes: C has no queue type, so the classic structure is written out: a fixed-size ring buffer with head/tail/count, one pthread_mutex_t for mutual exclusion and two condition variables (not_empty, not_full). put() locks, waits while the buffer is full (pthread_cond_wait with the predicate re-checked in a while loop - POSIX explicitly allows spurious wakeups), writes, and signals not_empty; take() mirrors it. Use pthread_cond_timedwait when a producer or consumer must not block forever, and make shutdown a flag that the waiting predicates also test followed by pthread_cond_broadcast, because a blocked condition wait cannot be released by setting a flag alone. Dijkstra's two-semaphore form (sem_t slots/items plus a binary semaphore guarding the buffer) is the alternative when POSIX semaphores are preferred over condition variables; C11 threads (mtx_t/cnd_t) offer the same shape portably.
pitfalls: A bare if around pthread_cond_wait is wrong: POSIX permits spurious wakeups, so every wait must sit in a while loop that re-checks the full/empty predicate on return.

Destroying or reusing the mutex/condition state while a thread is still blocked in a wait is undefined behavior; termination needs a checked flag plus pthread_cond_broadcast so each waiter can observe it and return.
Signalling without a predicate that the waiter re-checks can lose wakeups (or wake the wrong class of waiter); keep the state change and the signal ordered and let the loop decide.
The ring buffer copies items, so ownership of heap payloads must be explicit: freeing and reusing a buffer that is still queued is a use-after-free the compiler will not catch.
